brief.meaningEn: An organised way of storing and retrieving information in the mind.
brief.meaningZh: 在腦中有條理地儲存和提取資訊的方法。
brief.grammar: A clear set of notes can act as a mental filing system.
brief.register: Metaphor for an organised recall method; not a literal cabinet or simply a large amount of knowledge.
brief.boundaryZh: 重點是有條理地分類並能再找回資訊；與從記憶推得新理解不同。
brief.misconceptionZh: 別把任何零散筆記都稱為 filing system；必須有清楚的分類或檢索方法。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出如何分類資訊，以及日後如何迅速找回。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 31, row 3; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: A clear set of notes can act as a mental filing system.

listening.en: During the museum tour, Leo grouped facts about each room by period and theme. At revision time he could retrieve them easily; the groupings served as a mental filing system.
listening.zh: 參觀博物館時，里奧按年代與主題整理每個展廳的資料。溫習時他能輕易想起；那些分類成了他腦中的資料分類系統。
listening.promptZh: mental filing system 在這裏指甚麼？

options.en: His way of grouping facts so he could recall them later.
options.zh: 他把資料分組、方便日後回想的方法。

options.en: The museum’s catalogue, which he did not use to revise.
options.zh: 博物館的目錄，但他沒有用它溫習。

options.en: The number of facts he heard, whether organised or not.
options.zh: 他聽到的資料數量，不論有否整理。

options.en: His judgement about which historical period mattered most.
options.zh: 他對哪個歷史年代最重要的判斷。

listening.explanationZh: 他按年代和主題把資料歸類，方便提取；重點是記憶的組織方法，而非資料數量或對史實作出評價。

reply.promptEn: How does Maya remember the different plants she saw on field trips?
reply.promptZh: （瑪雅怎樣記住考察時見過的不同植物？）

options.en: She sorts them by habitat and keeps a clue for each group.
options.zh: 她按棲息地分類，並為每組留下提示。

options.en: She uses a few categories to bring the names back to mind.
options.zh: 她用幾個類別幫助自己想起名稱。

options.en: She has built a mental filing system based on habitat and leaf shape.
options.zh: 她按棲息地和葉形建立了腦中的資料分類系統。

options.en: She links each name to a category she can check later.
options.zh: 她把每個名稱連到日後可回想的類別。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都回答她如何分類及提取植物資料；金句用 mental filing system 概括組織方法。

options.en: Her categories form a mental filing system for recalling the events.
options.zh: 她的分類形成腦中的資料分類系統，方便回想活動。

options.en: She has memorised every sentence but has no way to locate a relevant event.
options.zh: 她記住所有句子，卻沒有方法找出相關活動。

options.en: She uses the dates to decide which exhibition was the most valuable.
options.zh: 她用日期判斷哪個展覽最有價值。

scene.explanationZh: 按主題及年份分類，使她能迅速提取資訊；題目未要求評價展覽價值。
scene.promptZh: 圖書館員先按主題、再按年份記住一批展覽資料，需要時便能迅速說出相關活動。哪句最貼切？

options.en: A gardener groups planting advice by season and retrieves the right tip later.
options.zh: 園丁按季節分類種植建議，日後能找回合適提示。

options.en: A visitor recalls many unrelated details but cannot link or retrieve the one requested.
options.zh: 訪客記得很多互不相關的細節，卻無法聯繫或找回所需資料。

options.en: A teacher associates each pupil’s name with a seating group and recalls it on request.
options.zh: 老師把每位學生的名字與座位組別聯繫，問起時能想起。

contrast.explanationZh: 資料多但欠缺可用分類、也無法提取，不足以稱為有條理的記憶系統。
contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不適合比喻為 mental filing system？

options.en: Try a mental filing system: group the events by month and type, then use those groups as clues.
options.zh: 試試在腦中分類：按月份和類型整理活動，再用類別作提示。

options.en: Keep memorising the same list without adding any categories or prompts.
options.zh: 繼續背同一份清單，不加分類或提示。

options.en: Judge which event was best before you work out when it happened.
options.zh: 先判斷哪項活動最好，再想它何時舉行。

dialogue.explanationZh: 朋友需要能找回活動的分類線索；另外兩句沒有解決檢索問題。
dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「我記得不少社區活動，但每次有人問去年辦了甚麼，我都想不起哪項在哪個月。」你怎樣建議較貼切？

speaking.en: Grouping memories by place gave her a mental filing system for recalling the trip.
speaking.zh: 按地點整理記憶，讓她有一套腦中的分類方法去回想旅程。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出資料如何歸類。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：學生要記住社區口述歷史訪談，原本把人物、地點和年份混在一起，回答時難以找回資料。她改為按地區及年代分類，然後用這些類別作回想線索。用一至兩句英文描述方法。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出原本資料混亂、改按地區及年代分類，以及分類如何幫她回想；不要只說她記住更多資料。

examples.en: Her mixed interview notes were hard to recall until she grouped them by district and decade, creating a mental filing system she could use to find each story.
examples.zh: 原本混雜的訪談筆記難以回想；她按地區和年代分類，建立一套腦中的資料分類系統，方便找回每個故事。

examples.en: By sorting the mixed interview notes into place and time categories, she built a mental filing system that helped her retrieve details when asked.
examples.zh: 她把原本混雜的訪談筆記按地點與時間分類，建立腦中的資料分類系統，問起時便能找回細節。

takeaways.en: A mental filing system helps me find the right example when I speak.
takeaways.zh: 腦中的資料分類系統能幫我說話時找出合適例子。

takeaways.en: Categories can create a mental filing system, but they work only if I can use them to recall details.
takeaways.zh: 類別可以構成腦中的資料分類系統，但必須能幫我回想細節才有用。

brief.meaningEn: Use what is remembered to understand a pattern or lesson, not merely repeat past facts.
brief.meaningZh: 運用記憶中的經驗，理解其中規律或教訓，而不只重述往事。
brief.grammar: Good questions can turn memory into insight.
brief.register: Analytical transformation pattern; state the recalled evidence and the new understanding drawn from it.
brief.boundaryZh: 與 mental filing system 的分類提取不同；本課需要從記起的事情得出理解或可行結論。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把單純懷舊或羅列日期說成 insight；要有新的理解。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出記起甚麼、比較或反思了甚麼，以及得出甚麼見解。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 31, row 9; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: Good questions can turn memory into insight.

listening.en: After three crowded school fairs, the committee compared where queues formed each year. They realised the entrance needed a second ticket desk. The comparison helped turn memory into insight.
listening.zh: 經歷三次擠迫的校園嘉年華後，委員會比較每年排隊的位置，發現入口需要多一個售票處。這番比較幫助他們把過往記憶化為洞見。
listening.promptZh: 委員會怎樣 turn memory into insight？

options.en: They used remembered queue patterns to identify a practical improvement.
options.zh: 他們利用記得的排隊情況，找出實際改善方法。

options.en: They listed fair dates without examining what happened at the entrance.
options.zh: 他們只列出嘉年華日期，沒有分析入口情況。

options.en: They chose a second desk before checking any past experience.
options.zh: 他們未參考過往經驗，便決定增設售票處。

options.en: They copied another fair’s desk arrangement without checking their own queue pattern.
options.zh: 他們未檢視自己的排隊情況，便照搬另一個嘉年華的櫃位安排。

listening.explanationZh: 他們回顧重複出現的排隊情況，得出增設售票處的可行見解；單純記日期或無證據猜測不足。

reply.promptEn: Why did the garden volunteers change their watering plan after the dry summers?
reply.promptZh: （連續幾個乾旱夏天後，園藝義工為何改變澆水計劃？）

options.en: They remembered which beds dried out first and shifted the watering times.
options.zh: 他們記得哪些花圃最先變乾，於是調整澆水時間。

options.en: They compared past results and identified when extra water was needed.
options.zh: 他們比較過去的結果，找出何時需要額外澆水。

options.en: They turned memory into insight by using the dry summers to improve the plan.
options.zh: 他們把乾旱夏天的經驗化為洞見，用來改善計劃。

options.en: They used what they had seen to target the driest beds earlier.
options.zh: 他們根據之前見到的情況，提早照顧最乾旱的花圃。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都從過往乾旱經驗引出具體改善；金句概括由記憶轉成理解的過程。

options.en: They turned memory into insight by linking the repeated problem to a sound check.
options.zh: 他們把記憶化為洞見，發現反覆出現的問題與音響檢查有關。

options.en: They remembered the dates of the performances but drew no conclusion.
options.zh: 他們記住演出日期，卻沒有得出結論。

options.en: They assumed the audience disliked the play without reviewing the sound records.
options.zh: 他們沒有翻查音響紀錄便斷言觀眾不喜歡劇本。

scene.explanationZh: 他們用重複發生的聽不清情況和紀錄得出音響改善方向，超越單純回憶。
scene.promptZh: 劇團記得前兩次演出時觀眾在換景期間聽不清對白，回看紀錄後發現音響需提前測試。哪句最貼切？

options.en: A coach compares past injuries and changes the warm-up to address a pattern.
options.zh: 教練比較過去的傷患個案，針對規律改變熱身。

options.en: An organiser recites old event dates but never asks what went well or wrong.
options.zh: 主辦者只背誦舊活動日期，從不反思成敗。

options.en: A student reflects on previous errors and spots a recurring misunderstanding.
options.zh: 學生反思以前的錯誤，找出反覆出現的誤解。

contrast.explanationZh: 只背日期未從經驗得出理解；另外兩項有比較或反思，並形成新見解。
contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不適合用 turn memory into insight？

options.en: Let us turn memory into insight by checking past queue times and moving the collection desk.
options.zh: 我們檢查過往排隊時間並調整收集櫃位，讓記憶化為洞見。

options.en: Since the events were busy, we already know exactly why every queue formed.
options.zh: 活動繁忙，所以我們已準確知道每條隊伍形成的原因。

options.en: We can write down the old dates and avoid reviewing how the desks were arranged.
options.zh: 我們可以記下舊日期，不用檢視櫃位怎樣安排。

dialogue.explanationZh: 回看具體時間與櫃位安排才可從記憶得出可用見解；只憑印象或列日期都不足。
dialogue.promptZh: 同事說：「去年每次捐贈書籍活動都在下午塞車，但我只記得人多，還沒有分析原因。」你怎樣回應最貼切？

speaking.en: By comparing old feedback, the organisers turned memory into insight and changed the next event.
speaking.zh: 主辦者比較舊評語，把過往記憶化為洞見，並改進下一次活動。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出回顧後得出的新理解。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社區巴士連續兩個冬季常有乘客錯過轉車。交通小組翻查投訴和班次紀錄，發現接駁時間不足，於是提議把其中一班巴士提早五分鐘。用一至兩句英文說明如何從過往經驗得出改善。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出兩個冬季的轉車問題、翻查投訴和班次後發現接駁時間不足，以及提早五分鐘的建議；不要只重述投訴。

examples.en: The transport team turned memory into insight by reviewing two winters of missed connections, finding that the transfer was too tight and proposing a bus five minutes earlier.
examples.zh: 交通小組翻查兩個冬季錯過轉車的紀錄，發現接駁時間太緊，提議把一班巴士提早五分鐘，把過往經驗化為洞見。

examples.en: After riders repeatedly missed the connection in winter, the team checked complaints and timetables, saw that the transfer gap was too short, and turned memory into insight: it proposed moving one bus five minutes earlier.
examples.zh: 連續兩個冬季都有乘客錯過轉車；小組翻查投訴及時間表，發現接駁時間太短，便把過往經驗化為洞見，提議把一班巴士提早五分鐘。

glossary.zh: 兩個冬季錯過轉車的紀錄

takeaways.en: Old records can turn memory into insight when we use them to find a pattern.
takeaways.zh: 若能從舊紀錄找出規律，便可把記憶化為洞見。

takeaways.en: Remembering a mistake is useful, but reflecting on it can turn memory into insight.
takeaways.zh: 記起錯誤有幫助；反思才能把記憶化為洞見。

notes: AI-authored provisional draft; independent English, Chinese, media and QA review remain pending.

brief.meaningEn: Have more mental demands or incoming information than one can comfortably handle.
brief.meaningZh: 腦中同時要處理太多要求或資訊，以致難以應付。
brief.grammar: Their minds are overloaded during the final week.
brief.register: Load metaphor for cognitive demands; show what is arriving at once and how it affects attention or recall.
brief.boundaryZh: 重點是同時承受的認知負荷過量；與 get cluttered 的思路雜亂不同，資料可以井然有序卻仍太多。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把一次普通分心或暫時忘記小事都診斷成 mind overloaded；須有可見的多重負擔。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出同時有哪些要求，以及負荷過重如何影響思考。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 32, row 2; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: Their minds are overloaded during the final week.

listening.en: At the event desk, two volunteers had to answer calls, check registrations and explain directions at the same time. Their minds were overloaded, so they asked a third person to handle the calls.
listening.zh: 活動接待處的兩名義工要同時接電話、核對登記和指路。他們腦中負荷過重，便請第三人處理來電。
listening.promptZh: 為何說義工的 minds were overloaded？

options.en: Several demands arrived at once and exceeded what two people could manage comfortably.
options.zh: 幾項要求同時到來，超出兩人能輕鬆處理的範圍。

options.en: Their directions were untidy even though they had no other tasks.
options.zh: 他們的指示不夠整齊，但沒有其他工作。

options.en: They had finished every registration before the phone rang.
options.zh: 電話響起前，他們已完成所有登記。

options.en: They chose to add another volunteer because the desk was empty.
options.zh: 接待處沒有人，所以他們決定增加義工。

listening.explanationZh: 電話、登記和指路同時需要注意力，兩人難以應付；請第三人接電話可分擔負荷。

reply.promptEn: Why did the reception team ask another volunteer to take phone calls?
reply.promptZh: （接待團隊為何請另一名義工接電話？）

options.en: They were checking arrivals and giving directions at the same time.
options.zh: 他們當時同時核對到場者並指路。

options.en: Several demands were competing for their attention.
options.zh: 幾項要求同時爭奪他們的注意力。

options.en: Their minds were overloaded by the tasks arriving together.
options.zh: 幾項任務一齊湧來，令他們腦中負荷過重。

options.en: Sharing the calls gave them room to focus on the people at the desk.
options.zh: 分擔來電後，他們可專注接待處的人。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都回答多項任務為何需要分工；金句指出同時處理的認知負荷過量。

options.en: The student’s mind is overloaded by several demands at once.
options.zh: 學生腦中同時要處理多項要求，已負荷過重。

options.en: The student has enough spare attention to follow every direction.
options.zh: 學生仍有充足注意力跟上每項指示。

options.en: The projector alone proves the student cannot organise any thoughts.
options.zh: 單靠投影設備便證明學生無法整理任何思緒。

scene.explanationZh: 同時要記錄、答問及操作設備，並開始漏聽指示，顯示負荷超出可處理範圍。
scene.promptZh: 學生同時要記講座要點、回答即席提問和操作投影設備，開始聽漏主持人的指示。哪句最貼切？

options.en: A worker misses a message while handling three urgent calls and a queue.
options.zh: 員工同時接三個緊急來電及應付排隊人龍，漏看一則訊息。

options.en: A visitor hears one clear instruction in a quiet room and follows it easily.
options.zh: 訪客在安靜房間聽到一項清楚指示，並輕易照做。

options.en: Students struggle to track several new rules introduced at the same moment.
options.zh: 幾條新規則同時公布，學生難以跟上。

contrast.explanationZh: 只有一項清楚要求而且能輕易完成，沒有負荷過量的證據。
contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不適合說 minds are overloaded？

options.en: Your mind may be overloaded; I can take the new queries while you greet visitors.
options.zh: 你可能已腦中負荷過重；我可接手新查詢，你先接待訪客。

options.en: You just need to remember every name without reducing the simultaneous tasks.
options.zh: 你只要記住每個姓名，毋須減少同時進行的工作。

options.en: The forgotten name proves visitors did not introduce themselves clearly.
options.zh: 忘記姓名證明訪客自我介紹時說得不清楚。

dialogue.explanationZh: 多項即時工作同時佔用注意力，分工能直接減輕負荷；另兩項忽略同時要求。
dialogue.promptZh: 同事說：「我一邊接待訪客，一邊處理三個即時查詢，現在連剛說過的姓名都記不起。」你如何回應較貼切？

speaking.en: Their minds were overloaded by the instructions arriving all at once.
speaking.zh: 指示一下子接連湧來，令他們腦中負荷過重。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出哪些要求同時出現。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：獸醫診所兩名護士同時要回答來電、整理藥物紀錄和處理現場預約，結果漏記了一個預約時間。診所安排第三名同事接手電話。用一至兩句英文描述原因與調整。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出三項同時任務令兩名護士負荷過重、漏記預約時間，以及第三人接電話如何分擔；不要把問題寫成必然記性差。

examples.en: The nurses’ minds were overloaded by calls, medicine records and bookings, so they missed an appointment time; a third colleague took over the phone.
examples.zh: 電話、藥物紀錄和預約令兩名護士腦中負荷過重，因此漏記一個預約時間；第三名同事接手電話。

examples.en: Their minds were overloaded while they handled calls, medicine records and in-person bookings, and one appointment time was missed; the clinic assigned another colleague to answer calls.
examples.zh: 兩名護士同時處理電話、藥物紀錄和現場預約，腦中負荷過重，漏記一個預約時間；診所安排另一名同事接電話。

takeaways.en: A single clear task may be easy even when our minds are overloaded by several simultaneous tasks.
takeaways.zh: 單一清楚任務可能容易處理；多項同時任務卻可能令腦中負荷過重。

takeaways.en: The students’ minds were overloaded when every new instruction arrived together.
takeaways.zh: 所有新指示同時到來，令學生腦中負荷過重。

brief.meaningEn: Become crowded and disorganised in one’s thoughts, making the main point hard to see.
brief.meaningZh: 思緒被雜亂的細節佔滿，令重點難以看清。
brief.grammar: My thinking can get cluttered after too many meetings.
brief.register: Metaphor from physical clutter; describe disorganisation of thinking, not merely heavy workload.
brief.boundaryZh: 與 minds are overloaded 不同：本課著眼於思路混雜、重點被埋沒，即使任務數量不多也可能發生。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要只因資訊多就說 cluttered；要見到內容零散、思路不清或重點難找。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出哪些互不相干的想法混在一起，以及如何重新理清重點。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 32, row 3; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: My thinking can get cluttered after too many meetings.

listening.en: Mei had ideas for a short speech, but she mixed examples, dates and side stories without a plan. Her thinking got cluttered, so she grouped the notes around one main point.
listening.zh: 美本來有一些短講想法，卻毫無規劃地混合例子、日期和枝節故事。她的思路變得雜亂，於是把筆記重新圍繞一個重點整理。
listening.promptZh: thinking got cluttered 表示甚麼？

options.en: Her ideas became disorganised and hid the main point.
options.zh: 她的想法變得雜亂，掩蓋了重點。

options.en: She had too many urgent tasks to complete on the same day.
options.zh: 她同一天要完成太多緊急任務。

options.en: She found a clear order for every example before writing.
options.zh: 她寫作前已為每個例子找到清楚次序。

options.en: The dates she used were inaccurate and needed verification.
options.zh: 她使用的日期不準確，需要核實。

listening.explanationZh: 例子、日期和枝節混在一起，使主線不清；問題是思路雜亂，不必然是任務過多或日期有誤。

reply.promptEn: Why did Amir rewrite his presentation outline?

options.en: His notes mixed the central claim with unrelated anecdotes.
options.zh: 他的筆記把核心論點和無關軼事混在一起。

options.en: He wanted the main argument to stand out from side details.
options.zh: 他希望主論點能從枝節中突顯出來。

options.en: His thinking had got cluttered, so he reorganised the examples.
options.zh: 他的思路變得雜亂，因此重新整理例子。

options.en: He grouped related points to make the argument easier to follow.
options.zh: 他把相關要點歸類，令論述更易理解。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明主線被雜亂枝節掩蓋，重寫是為了理清思路；金句用 cluttered 概括。

options.en: The student’s thinking got cluttered, and the main conclusion was buried.
options.zh: 學生的思路變得雜亂，主要結論被掩蓋。

options.en: The main conclusion was clear because the stories were unrelated.
options.zh: 故事互不相關，所以主要結論很清楚。

options.en: The student was handling several urgent jobs at once, leaving no time to speak.
options.zh: 學生同時處理數項緊急工作，沒有時間演講。

scene.explanationZh: 問題是互不相關的故事混在一起，讓主線不清；並非有多項工作同時壓身。
scene.promptZh: 學生準備一個五分鐘報告，將三個互不相關的故事混進同一段，聽眾無法聽出主要結論。哪句最貼切？

options.en: A writer mixes three unrelated themes in one paragraph and loses the point.
options.zh: 作者把三個無關主題混在一段，令重點模糊。

options.en: A speaker has one clear argument, ordered examples and a concise conclusion.
options.zh: 講者有一個清楚論點、按次序排列的例子及簡潔結論。

options.en: A student’s notes mix side comments with key evidence until neither stands out.
options.zh: 學生把枝節評語與重要證據混雜，兩者都不突出。

contrast.explanationZh: 論點、例子和結論都清楚有序，沒有思路雜亂的跡象。
contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不適合用 get cluttered 描述思路？

options.en: Your thinking may have got cluttered; choose one message and group only the relevant stories around it.
options.zh: 你的思路可能變得雜亂；先選一個重點，只把相關故事放在一起。

options.en: Keep every side story in the same paragraph, so no memory is omitted.
options.zh: 把每個枝節故事留在同一段，才不會漏掉回憶。

options.en: The problem must be that you have too many separate tasks, not the order of your ideas.
options.zh: 問題一定是你有太多不同工作，而不是想法排列的次序。

dialogue.explanationZh: 朋友明說枝節太多且主旨失焦，應整理相關故事；其餘回應沒有處理思路混雜。
dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「我的演講稿把每個回憶和旁枝故事都放進去了，現在連主要訊息也找不到。」你如何回應最貼切？

speaking.en: When unrelated examples filled my notes, my thinking got cluttered and I lost the main point.
speaking.zh: 互不相關的例子填滿筆記時，我的思路變得雜亂，失去重點。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出哪種資訊混亂造成問題。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：學生要寫社區花園介紹，原本把種植方法、義工名單和活動日期全部塞進同一段，讀者看不出花園的主要特色。學生按主題重排內容。用一至兩句英文描述問題和改善。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出三類內容原本混雜、主要特色不清，以及按主題重排後如何突出重點；不要只說內容多。

examples.en: Her thinking got cluttered when she mixed planting tips, volunteer names and event dates in one paragraph; grouping the ideas by topic made the garden’s main feature clear.
examples.zh: 她擬寫花園介紹時，把種植貼士、義工名單和活動日期混在同一段，思路變得雜亂；按主題整理後，花園主要特色便清楚了。

examples.en: Her thinking got cluttered as she mixed planting methods with names and dates, so she separated the topics and brought the garden’s main feature forward.
examples.zh: 她把種植方法、人名和日期混在一起，思路變得雜亂；她遂把主題分開，讓花園主要特色更突出。

takeaways.en: An outline helps me when my thinking gets cluttered by unrelated details.
takeaways.zh: 無關枝節令我思路雜亂時，大綱可幫我整理。

takeaways.en: Grouping the notes by topic stopped my thinking from getting cluttered.
takeaways.zh: 按主題分類筆記，令我的思路不再變得雜亂。
